        - paragraph: In simple English
        - heading "Understand One-Sided Limits" [level=2]
        - paragraph: "A one-sided limit describes what a function approaches from only the left or only the right. In One-Sided Limits, that statement is the exact rule used on the labelled chart and in the three numerical examples. A useful rule is One-sided limits: lim x->a- f(x), lim x->a+ f(x). You can learn One-Sided Limits by trying one small example instead of long theory."
        - paragraph: Approach the point from the left. Record the output trend. Approach from the right and compare. Try the example below. Write your steps and choose an answer before opening the comparison.
        - paragraph: "In real life, piecewise prices: A rule can jump at a boundary. Watch out: Using one side to claim a two-sided limit. Check both sides."
